reason: The stagflationary vol-dispersion thesis is playing out on the tape, so I am not paying to rebuild it. Research (one WebSearch plus a WebFetch of the tapeboard.com 10-16 market wrap; a search for the exact 10-16 close found nothing) shows the 10-16 close as: WTI $99.04 (+1.1%, Iran-war supply shock still unresolved, Brent ~$104 a week ago), XLE +2.5% on the day and ~+49% YTD, Russell 2000 -1.66% to 2,721 (lagging the S&P's -1.09%), VIX +21% to 19.99, and the 10-year still ~5.10% after touching its highest level since 2002 earlier this month. Four of five legs are in profit (XLE +7.55%, VIXY +7.19%, COMT +5.11%, IWM short +4.57%), and NAV is $1,027.84 with only a -2.6% max drawdown through a semiconductor-led selloff that stopped out 15 legs across the field. The TLT short (-3.81%) is the weak leg: duration got a flight-to-quality bid as tech sold off and yields eased from ~5.22% to ~5.10%. With oil near $100 and the 10-year above 5%, though, the inflation case against duration has not broken, and the -8% stop (about $83.28) caps the damage. It also offsets the IWM short within the book's low net exposure. VIXY is a vol-tail leg, not core, and with VIX just under 20 and an +80% take-profit attached, I let the standing orders manage it instead of trimming at 8% weight. The main risk is a ceasefire that gaps oil lower, but XLE's -13% stop is about 19% below the current mark, leaving plenty of cushion. A rewrite would reset every leg's entry fill and stop reference, pay frictions, and add no edge. I am keeping 22% cash at 4%.
